      rcases hgood.1 (w n) hgood.2.2 (hwzero n) with honline | hperiod
      · exact False.elim (hgood.2.1 honline)

      intro hall

    exact xiC_no_vertical_zero_progression z hTpos' hprog

      rw [mul_assoc]

by

  have hrect : ∀ T : ℝ,
      ((∫ x : ℝ in c..d, G ((x : ℂ) + ((-T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I))
          - (∫ x : ℝ in c..d, G ((x : ℂ) + ((T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I))
          + I • (∫ y : ℝ in (-T)..T, G ((d : ℂ) + (y : ℝ) * I)))

    intro T
    have hz : ((c : ℂ) + ((-T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I).re = c := by simp
    have hz' : ((c : ℂ) + ((-T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I).im = -T := by simp
    have hw : ((d : ℂ) + ((T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I).re = d := by simp
    have hw' : ((d : ℂ) + ((T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I).im = T := by simp
    have hsub : DifferentiableOn ℂ G
        (uIcc ((c : ℂ) + ((-T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I).re ((d : ℂ) + ((T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I).re ×ℂ
          uIcc ((c : ℂ) + ((-T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I).im ((d : ℂ) + ((T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I).im) := by
      rw [hz, hz', hw, hw']
      exact hdiff.mono (rect_subset_verticalStrip hcd T)

      ((c : ℂ) + ((-T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I) ((d : ℂ) + ((T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I) hsub
    rw [hz, hz', hw, hw'] at hcauchy

      (𝓝 (∫ y : ℝ, G ((d : ℂ) + (y : ℝ) * I))) :=
    intervalIntegral_tendsto_integral hd tendsto_neg_atTop_atBot tendsto_id
  have hlimc : Tendsto (fun T : ℝ => ∫ y : ℝ in (-T)..T, G ((c : ℂ) + (y : ℝ) * I)) atTop
      (𝓝 (∫ y : ℝ, G ((c : ℂ) + (y : ℝ) * I))) :=
    intervalIntegral_tendsto_integral hc tendsto_neg_atTop_atBot tendsto_id
  have hcomb := ((hbot.sub htop).add (hlimd.const_smul I)).sub (hlimc.const_smul I)
  have hzero : Tendsto (fun T : ℝ =>
      ((∫ x : ℝ in c..d, G ((x : ℂ) + ((-T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I))
          - (∫ x : ℝ in c..d, G ((x : ℂ) + ((T : ℝ) : ℂ) * I))
          + I • (∫ y : ℝ in (-T)..T, G ((d : ℂ) + (y : ℝ) * I)))
        - I • (∫ y : ℝ in (-T)..T, G ((c : ℂ) + (y : ℝ) * I))) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    simp only [hrect]
    exact tendsto_const_nhds
  have heq := tendsto_nhds_unique hcomb hzero
  have hI : I * ((∫ y : ℝ, G ((d : ℂ) + (y : ℝ) * I)) - ∫ y : ℝ, G ((c : ℂ) + (y : ℝ) * I))

    rw [mul_zero, mul_sub]
    simpa [smul_eq_mul] using heq

  linear_combination this

# Hypertranscendence of Gamma self-composition

- **ID:** gamma-self-composition-hypertranscendence
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM · HYPERTRANSCENDENCE
- **Status:** `[PROVEN] [LEAN FORMALIZED] [CANDIDATE NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]`
- **Statement:** The self-composite `z ↦ Γ(Γ(z))` is hypertranscendental.  Stronger, no algebraic
  differential relation holds on any nonempty open patch of its regular set.

## Proof mechanism

The generic Gamma factorial constraint-reflection theorem gives the implication

\[
\Gamma\circ\Gamma\ \text{differentially algebraic}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\Gamma\ \text{satisfies one nonzero polynomial jet relation on }\Re z>0.
\]

Any such local relation for Gamma continues across the connected complement of its poles.  Multiply
the continued relation by the order-zero Gamma jet: off the poles the original relation vanishes,
and at every pole mathlib's totalized Gamma value is zero.  This produces a global nonzero
differential polynomial annihilating Gamma, contradicting the formal Hölder theorem.

For the local strengthening, the regular set is

\[
\Omega_{\Gamma\circ\Gamma}
=\{z:\Gamma(z)\notin\{0,-1,-2,\ldots\}\}.
\]

It is the already formalized regular set used for `ψ ∘ Γ`: its complement is countable and it is
path connected.  A relation on one nonempty regular open patch therefore propagates to every late
factorial microscope.  The microscope-local Gamma reflection theorem then yields the same forbidden
right-half-plane relation for the outer Gamma germ.

## Why this crosses the old wall

The backlog route correctly killed abstract `HT ∘ HT` closure, Nevanlinna-order arguments, and
finite chain-rule manipulations.  The factorial proof is source-specific: it uses the exact pole
residues `(-1)^n/n!`, a static highest-weight/point-degree initial form, and the Möbius limit
`x ↦ -1/x`.  It never evaluates a generic outer relation at an uncontrolled transcendental point.

# Hypertranscendence of every finite Gamma iterate

- **ID:** finite-gamma-iteration-hypertranscendence
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM · ITERATION HYPERTRANSCENDENCE
- **Status:** `[PROVEN] [LEAN FORMALIZED] [CANDIDATE NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]`
- **Statement:** Let `F₀(z)=z` and `Fₖ₊₁(z)=Γ(Fₖ(z))`.  For every `k ≥ 1`, the germ of
  `Fₖ` at the Gamma fixed point `1` admits no nonzero polynomial-coefficient differential relation.
  Consequently every finite Gamma iterate is hypertranscendental.

## Source-pure mechanism

The point `1` is fixed by Gamma, and every finite iterate is analytic on some neighborhood of `1`.
At the factorial poles of the innermost Gamma,

\[
  \Gamma\!\left(-n+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n!}x\right)\longrightarrow -\frac1x.
\]

Thus a hypothetical local differential relation for `Fₖ₊₁ = Fₖ ∘ Γ`, propagated to all late
microscopes, has a nonzero initial form annihilating `x ↦ Fₖ(-1/x)`.  Möbius jet pullback turns it
into a nonzero local relation for `Fₖ` near `1`, contradicting the induction hypothesis.  The
argument uses only a small microscope neighborhood of `x=-1`; unlike the first global composition
principle, it must not assume that `Fₖ` is analytic on the whole right half-plane.

## Local reflection core `[PROVEN]`

Localize the factorial initial-form theorem and the outer-composition jet-convergence theorem to an
arbitrary open microscope patch `U` containing `-1`, under analyticity of the outer germ on a
neighborhood of `-1/U`.  Prove that the existing triangular Möbius pullback remains injective and
that the resulting relation holds eventually near `1`.  Then package the fixed-point induction.

This is an analytic localization of the concrete Gamma microscope, not a new carrier or abstract
constraint-reflector class.

The localization is realized using the intrinsic domain

\[
  U_\Omega=\{x\ne0:-1/x\in\Omega\},
\]

where `Ω` is the outer germ's open regular set.  Compact-open Gamma convergence keeps every late
microscope inside `Ω`; Cauchy jet convergence produces the initial relation; the local Möbius
pullback contradicts rigidity at `1`.

For the induction, the depth-`k` regular set is defined recursively by requiring the innermost
Gamma input to avoid its poles and its value to lie in the depth-`k-1` regular set.  Every Gamma
fiber is countable, so every finite-depth singular complement is countable and the regular set is
path connected.  A relation on any regular patch therefore propagates to the microscope domain.

## Stronger route kept separate

Differential algebraic independence of `(F₁,…,Fₖ)` would be substantially stronger.  One microscope
lowers every depth by one, but the first component degenerates to the rational germ `-1/x`; a
nonzero multivariate initial polynomial may therefore enter the differential ideal of that rational
germ.  Defeating this kernel requires a source-specific higher residue or deformation invariant and
is not implied by the single-function induction above.

  their algebraic differential equations.

## Public sentence

An isolated quantum system can reach its far future cheaply only by returning
to a past it could already reach cheaply.

## What was missing

Recurrence and circuit complexity have been treated as separate observables:
one asks whether a state comes back, the other whether a circuit can prepare
it.  The failed static Krylov-load route shows why that separation is wrong.
A time-independent carrier recognizes that a target belongs to the orbit's
polynomial history, but forgets *where in time* it belongs.  An easy past
state then looks like a permanent future shortcut even when its late overlap
is zero.

The missing primitive is therefore an **oriented circuit--orbit relation**.
It records both preparation cost and lag.  Complexity growth, plateau, and
recurrence are proposed to be three shadows of one statement: after quotienting
by genuine returns, autonomous time is an injective local computation.

## Frozen conjecture

Fix `q>=2`, a finite universal two-qubit gate alphabet, trace-distance
resolution `epsilon`, and the normalized full bounded-weight Gaussian Pauli
ensemble

\[
 H_{n,q}=\sum_{1\leq |P|\leq q}J_PP .                  \tag{1}
\]

Let `Phi_H(t)` be its normalized Choi orbit and let `Lambda(H)` be the explicit
interaction-rate normalization used by the matching product-formula upper
bound.  There are constants `a,A,c>0`, depending only on `q`, gate alphabet,
and fixed resolution, such that with probability at least
`1-exp(-c m)` over `H`, simultaneously for every pre-recurrence time `t` and
every circuit budget `s<=a Lambda(H)t`,

\[
 \boxed{
 C_\epsilon(\Phi_H(t))\leq s
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \exists u\in[0,A s/\Lambda(H)] :
 d_{\rm tr}(\Phi_H(t),\Phi_H(u))\leq 2\epsilon . }
                                                               \tag{ONS}
\]

Equivalently, every intersection between the late autonomous orbit and the
`s`-gate tube is generated by a spectral return to the initial orbit segment
which `s` gates can already reach by ordinary forward simulation.  A short
circuit is never a third mechanism.

The quantifiers in `(ONS)` are part of the conjecture.  `Pre-recurrence` means
the explicit finite-size interval ending at the first `2epsilon` return to the
simulable segment; it is not a hypothesis that assumes absence of shortcuts.

## Immediate consequences if true

1. **Ballistic growth.**  Before the first return to the simulable segment,
   `(ONS)` gives `C_epsilon(Phi_H(t))>a Lambda(H)t`; product-formula simulation
   supplies the matching upper rate up to stated polynomial factors.
2. **Plateau.**  After `a Lambda t` reaches state-space circuit capacity, the
   completed spectral-torus volume law makes returns to every submaximal
   simulable segment quantitatively rare, so complexity is maximal for density
   one.
3. **Recurrence.**  The first post-plateau low-complexity time is exactly the
   first spectral return to an earlier simulable segment.  Existing torus
   return-volume laws then set its doubly exponential scale.
4. **No-fast-forwarding classification.**  A genuine fast-forwarding family
   must create an off-diagonal component of the oriented relation.  Commuting,
   free, and finite-order models are exceptional because they do exactly that.
5. **Complexity without Haar randomness.**  The permanent local two-query
   witness remains valid on the same Hamiltonian at every time; `(ONS)` does
   not identify maximal complexity with Haar statistics.

namespace RHTower

open Complex Metric Set

/-! ### §1 Indexed configurations as list splits -/

/-- The list of an indexed configuration: each centre repeated with its
multiplicity. -/
def configList {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (ρc : ι → ℂ) (m : ι → ℕ) : List ℂ :=
  s.toList.flatMap fun i => List.replicate (m i) (ρc i)

theorem configList_length {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (ρc : ι → ℂ) (m : ι → ℕ) :
    (configList s ρc m).length = ∑ i ∈ s, m i := by
  rw [configList, List.length_flatMap]
  simp only [List.length_replicate]
  exact Finset.sum_map_toList s m

theorem configList_map_prod {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (ρc : ι → ℂ) (m : ι → ℕ)
    (z : ℂ) :
    ((configList s ρc m).map (fun w => z - w)).prod
      = ∏ i ∈ s, (z - ρc i) ^ m i := by
  rw [configList, List.map_flatMap, ← Finset.prod_map_toList]
  induction s.toList with
  | nil => simp
  | cons a l ih =>
    simp only [List.flatMap_cons, List.prod_append, List.map_cons,
      List.prod_cons, List.map_replicate, List.prod_replicate]
    rw [← ih]
    simp [List.map_replicate]

theorem configList_mem {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {ρc : ι → ℂ} {m : ι → ℕ}
    {ρ : ℂ} {r₀ : ℝ} (hρ : ∀ i ∈ s, ‖ρc i - ρ‖ ≤ r₀) :
    ∀ w ∈ configList s ρc m, ‖w - ρ‖ ≤ r₀ := by
  intro w hw
  rw [configList, List.mem_flatMap] at hw
  obtain ⟨i, hi, hwi⟩ := hw
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := List.mem_replicate.mp hwi
  exact hρ i (Finset.mem_toList.mp hi)

/-- **The count identity, configuration form**: the total multiplicity of any
enclosed configuration of any member dominating ξ on the charts of an isolating
annulus is the central ξ-order. -/
theorem enclosed_configuration_count_of_domination {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (ρc : ι → ℂ) (m : ι → ℕ) {F u : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ : ℂ} {r₀ R : ℝ}
    (h0 : 0 ≤ r₀) (hrR : r₀ < R)

    (hu_an : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ u (ball ρ R)) (hu_ne : ∀ z ∈ ball ρ R, u z ≠ 0)
    (hfact : ∀ z ∈ chartRA ρ r₀ R ∪ chartLA ρ r₀ R,

  intro z hz

Assembling the admissibility package with the slice preparation theorem: a holomorphic function
near the origin of `ℂ^(n+1)` whose slice in the distinguished variable is not identically zero is,
on a polydisc, a *distinguished* monic polynomial in that variable — coefficients holomorphic in
the parameters and vanishing at the origin — times a nowhere vanishing holomorphic unit.

The coefficients are the elementary symmetric functions of the moving root multiset, and at the
origin every root is the origin, because the radius was chosen so that the slice has no other zero
in the closed disc.

/-- Every element of a replicated multiset of zeros is zero, so all its higher elementary
symmetric functions vanish. -/
theorem esymm_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero {M : Multiset ℂ} (hM : ∀ r ∈ M, r = 0) {k : ℕ}
    (hk : 0 < k) : M.esymm k = 0 := by
  classical
  rw [Multiset.esymm]
  refine Multiset.sum_eq_zero ?_
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩ := Multiset.mem_map.mp hx
  have hsub : s ≤ M := (Multiset.mem_powersetCard.mp hs).1
  have hcard : Multiset.card s = k := (Multiset.mem_powersetCard.mp hs).2
  have hne : s ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    rw [h] at hcard
    simp only [Multiset.card_zero] at hcard
    omega
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := Multiset.exists_mem_of_ne_zero hne
  have hr0 : r = 0 := hM r (Multiset.mem_of_le hsub hr)
  exact Multiset.prod_eq_zero (by rwa [hr0] at hr)

/-- **The roots of the slice at the origin all sit at the origin.** -/
theorem sliceRoots_eq_zero_of_isolated {f : (Fin (n + 1) → ℂ) → ℂ} {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t)

    (hiso : ∀ z : ℂ, z ≠ 0 → ‖z‖ ≤ t → f (Fin.cons z (0 : Fin n → ℂ)) ≠ 0) :

  intro r hr
  by_contra hr0
  have hlt : ‖r‖ < t := sliceRoots_norm_lt ht hadm r hr
  exact hiso r hr0 hlt.le ((slice_eq_zero_iff_mem_sliceRoots ht hadm hlt).mpr hr)

/-- **Weierstrass preparation of a germ.**  A holomorphic function whose slice in the distinguished
variable is not identically zero near the origin factors on a polydisc as a distinguished monic
polynomial times a nowhere vanishing unit. -/
theorem germ_weierstrass_preparation {f : (Fin (n + 1) → ℂ) → ℂ}
    {U : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℂ)} (hU : IsOpen U) (h0 : (0 : Fin (n + 1) → ℂ) ∈ U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    (hreg : ¬ (fun z : ℂ => f (Fin.cons z (0 : Fin n → ℂ))) =ᶠ[𝓝 (0 : ℂ)] 0) :
    ∃ (t δ : ℝ) (d : ℕ) (a : ℕ → (Fin n → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : (Fin (n + 1) → ℂ) → ℂ),
      0 < t ∧ 0 < δ ∧
      (∀ j, DifferentiableOn ℂ (a j) (ball (0 : Fin n → ℂ) δ)) ∧
      (∀ j, j < d → a j (0 : Fin n → ℂ) = 0) ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℂ u
        {w : Fin (n + 1) → ℂ | Fin.tail w ∈ ball (0 : Fin n → ℂ) δ ∧ ‖w 0‖ < t} ∧
      (∀ y ∈ ball (0 : Fin n → ℂ) δ, ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ < t →
        f (Fin.cons z y)
            = (z ^ d + ∑ j ∈ Finset.range d, a j y * z ^ j) * u (Fin.cons z y)
          ∧ u (Fin.cons z y) ≠ 0) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨t, δ, htpos, hδpos, hdisc2, hdisc, hnez, hadm, hiso⟩ :=
    exists_sliceAdmissible_nhds hU h0 hf hreg
  set V : Set (Fin n → ℂ) := ball (0 : Fin n → ℂ) δ with hV
  have hVopen : IsOpen V := isOpen_ball
  have hVconn : IsPreconnected V := (convex_ball (0 : Fin n → ℂ) δ).isPreconnected
  have h0V : (0 : Fin n → ℂ) ∈ V := mem_ball_self hδpos
  set d : ℕ := Multiset.card (sliceRoots f t (0 : Fin n → ℂ)) with hd
  have hcard : ∀ y ∈ V, Multiset.card (sliceRoots f t y) = d := fun y hy =>
    card_sliceRoots_const_of_isPreconnected hU hVopen hf htpos hdisc hnez hadm hVconn hy h0V
  refine ⟨t, δ, d, fun j y => (-1) ^ (d - j) * (sliceRoots f t y).esymm (d - j),
    sliceUnit f t, htpos, hδpos, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro j
    exact ((differentiableOn_esymm_sliceRoots hU hVopen hf htpos hdisc hnez hadm
      (d - j)).const_mul ((-1 : ℂ) ^ (d - j)))
  · intro j hj
    have hzero : (sliceRoots f t (0 : Fin n → ℂ)).esymm (d - j) = 0 :=
      esymm_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero
        (sliceRoots_eq_zero_of_isolated htpos (hadm _ h0V) hiso) (by omega)
    show (-1 : ℂ) ^ (d - j) * (sliceRoots f t (0 : Fin n → ℂ)).esymm (d - j) = 0
    rw [hzero, mul_zero]
  · exact differentiableOn_sliceUnit hU hVopen hf htpos hdisc hnez hadm hVconn h0V
  · intro y hy z hz
    obtain ⟨hfact, hune⟩ :=
      (weierstrass_preparation hU hVopen hf htpos hdisc hnez hadm hVconn h0V).2.2 y hy z hz
    refine ⟨?_, hune⟩
    rw [hfact, sliceWeierstrass_cons, multisetLinearProd_eq_monic, hcard y hy]

theorem mem_semiRiemannianRadical_iff_pairing_zero_on_total

    {g : BilinForm K V} (hnd : g.Nondegenerate) (hrefl : g.IsRefl)
    {vertical : Submodule K V} {v : V} :

  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hvV, hvH⟩ u hu
    have hu' : u ∈ vertical ⊔ semiRiemannianHorizontal g vertical := by
      simpa [semiRiemannianTotal] using hu
    rcases Submodule.mem_sup.mp hu' with ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
    have hva : g v a = 0 :=
      hrefl a v ((LinearMap.BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff.mp hvH) a ha)
    have hvb : g v b = 0 :=
      (LinearMap.BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff.mp hb) v hvV
    simp [hva, hvb]
  · intro hall
    constructor
    · have hvHH : v ∈ g.orthogonal (g.orthogonal vertical) := by
        rw [LinearMap.BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff]
        intro h hh
        exact hrefl v h (hall h (show h ∈ semiRiemannianTotal g vertical from
          Submodule.mem_sup_right hh))
      rw [LinearMap.BilinForm.orthogonal_orthogonal hnd hrefl] at hvHH
      exact hvHH
    · exact LinearMap.BilinForm.mem_orthogonal_iff.mpr (by
        intro a ha
        exact hrefl v a (hall a (show a ∈ semiRiemannianTotal g vertical from
          Submodule.mem_sup_left ha)))

/-- Phase-coordinate form of a nonzero Smirnov Toeplitz-kernel element.  Inner--outer
factorization gives a nondecreasing inner phase `α`; Kolmogorov's theorem makes the regularized
Hilbert transform of the outer logarithm sublinear. -/
structure SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness (γ : ℝ → ℝ) where
  innerPhase : ℝ → ℝ
  outerHilbertPhase : ℝ → ℝ
  innerPhase_monotone : Monotone innerPhase
  phase_balance : ∀ x, γ x + innerPhase x = outerHilbertPhase x
  outerHilbertPhase_sublinear_atTop :
    Tendsto (fun x => outerHilbertPhase x / x) atTop (nhds 0)

def SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness.add {γ δ : ℝ → ℝ}
    (Wγ : SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness γ)
    (Wδ : SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness δ) :
    SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness (fun x => γ x + δ x) where
  innerPhase := fun x => Wγ.innerPhase x + Wδ.innerPhase x
  outerHilbertPhase := fun x => Wγ.outerHilbertPhase x + Wδ.outerHilbertPhase x
  innerPhase_monotone := Wγ.innerPhase_monotone.add Wδ.innerPhase_monotone
  phase_balance := by
    intro x
    rw [show γ x + δ x + (Wγ.innerPhase x + Wδ.innerPhase x) =
      (γ x + Wγ.innerPhase x) + (δ x + Wδ.innerPhase x) by ring,
      Wγ.phase_balance, Wδ.phase_balance]
  outerHilbertPhase_sublinear_atTop := by
    convert Wγ.outerHilbertPhase_sublinear_atTop.add
      Wδ.outerHilbertPhase_sublinear_atTop using 1
    · funext x
      rw [add_div]
    · ring

def SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness.congr {γ δ : ℝ → ℝ}
    (W : SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness γ) (h : ∀ x, γ x = δ x) :
    SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness δ where
  innerPhase := W.innerPhase
  outerHilbertPhase := W.outerHilbertPhase
  innerPhase_monotone := W.innerPhase_monotone
  phase_balance := by intro x; rw [← h x, W.phase_balance]
  outerHilbertPhase_sublinear_atTop := W.outerHilbertPhase_sublinear_atTop

theorem tendsto_div_atTop_zero_of_abs_le
    {f : ℝ → ℝ} {C : ℝ} (hf : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) :
    Tendsto (fun x => f x / x) atTop (nhds 0) := by
  rw [Metric.tendsto_atTop]
  intro ε hε
  refine ⟨max 1 (C / ε + 1), ?_⟩
  intro x hx
  rw [Real.dist_eq]
  have hx0 : 0 < x := lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one
    (le_trans (le_max_left 1 (C / ε + 1)) hx)
  have hCdiv : C / x < ε := by
    have hxC : C / ε < x := lt_of_lt_of_le (lt_add_one (C / ε))
      (le_trans (le_max_right 1 (C / ε + 1)) hx)
    apply (div_lt_iff₀ hx0).2
    simpa [mul_comm] using (div_lt_iff₀ hε).mp hxC
  rw [sub_zero, abs_div, abs_of_pos hx0]
  exact lt_of_le_of_lt (div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (hf x) hx0.le) hCdiv

/-- Smirnov--Kolmogorov bounded-phase multiplier at exponent `p = 1/2`, in phase coordinates. -/
noncomputable def boundedPhaseBlaschkeFourWitness (b : ℝ → ℝ) (C : ℝ) (_hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hb : ∀ x, |b x| ≤ C) :
    SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness (fun x => -8 * Real.arctan x + 2 * b x) where
  innerPhase := fun x => 8 * Real.arctan x
  outerHilbertPhase := fun x => 2 * b x
  innerPhase_monotone := ((show StrictMono Real.arctan from
    fun _ _ h => Real.arctan_lt_arctan_iff.mpr h).const_mul
      (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 8)).monotone
  phase_balance := by intro x; ring
  outerHilbertPhase_sublinear_atTop := by
    apply tendsto_div_atTop_zero_of_abs_le (C := 2 * C)
    intro x
    rw [abs_mul]
    simpa only [abs_of_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)] using
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hb x) (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)

/-- Makarov--Poltoratski upper-density obstruction at `κ = 0`, in the exact phase criterion:
a Toeplitz phase whose excess over the exponential inner phase grows to `+∞` cannot have a
nonzero Smirnov kernel element. -/
theorem not_smirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness_of_sub_id_tendsto_atTop
    {γ : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hgrowth : Tendsto (fun x => γ x - x) atTop atTop) :
    ¬ Nonempty (SmirnovToeplitzPhaseWitness γ) := by
  rintro ⟨W⟩
  have houter : ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, W.outerHilbertPhase x / x < (1 / 4 : ℝ) :=
    W.outerHilbertPhase_sublinear_atTop.eventually
      (Iio_mem_nhds (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 4))
  have hinner : ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, W.innerPhase 0 ≤ W.innerPhase x :=
    (eventually_ge_atTop 0).mono fun x hx => W.innerPhase_monotone hx
  have hxpos : ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, 0 < x := eventually_gt_atTop 0
  have hlarge : ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, 4 * |W.innerPhase 0| < x :=
    eventually_gt_atTop (4 * |W.innerPhase 0|)
  have hgrowth0 : ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, 0 < γ x - x :=
    hgrowth.eventually (eventually_gt_atTop 0)
  have hall : ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
      W.outerHilbertPhase x / x < (1 / 4 : ℝ) ∧
      W.innerPhase 0 ≤ W.innerPhase x ∧ 0 < x ∧
      4 * |W.innerPhase 0| < x ∧ 0 < γ x - x := by
    filter_upwards [houter, hinner, hxpos, hlarge, hgrowth0] with x ho hi hx hl hg
    exact ⟨ho, hi, hx, hl, hg⟩
  obtain ⟨x, ho, hi, hx, hl, hg⟩ := hall.exists
  have houter_lt : W.outerHilbertPhase x < x / 4 :=
    by
      have := (div_lt_iff₀ hx).mp (by simpa using ho)
      simpa [div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm] using this
  have hinner_lower : -x / 4 < W.innerPhase x := by

/-!
# Where independence acts in the favourable direction: self-recurrence

Multiplicative independence of the primes is the only property separating zeta from the
functional-equation counterexamples, but its one exact consequence in this development — the
decoupling of the prime symbol's extremes — *maximises* the prime side and therefore works against
positivity.  This file records where it acts the other way.

**The conjecture that fails.**  An off-critical zero does **not** impose a `ℚ`-linear relation among
the prime logarithms.  A zero is a location in the plane; nothing transports it into an additive
relation among `log p`, and the growth it forces on the prime-counting error is an `Ω`-result, not a
contradiction.  So independence cannot exclude off-line zeros directly.

**Where it does act favourably.**  Independence gives equidistribution of the phases `(t log p)_p`,
hence approximation of prescribed values by translates `ζ(s + iτ)` — the universality phenomenon.
Universality approximates every **non-vanishing** analytic function on a compact set in the strip.
Whether `ζ` itself is among them is exactly whether `ζ` is non-vanishing there.  That is the
favourable direction: independence supplies the approximation, and the hypothesis is the statement
that `ζ` may approximate itself.

**The mechanism, and it is a counting contradiction.**  Suppose `ζ` had a zero inside a disc `K` in
the strip, and suppose translates `ζ(· + iτ)` approximated `ζ` on `K` to within the minimum of `|ζ|`
on `∂K` for a set of `τ` of positive density.  Each such translate then has a zero in `K` by the
sphere-domination principle, so the zeros of `ζ` in that vertical strip have **positive density in
`T`** — while the zero-counting function in any strip `σ > 1/2 + δ` grows more slowly than linearly.
The two are incompatible.

> **Self-recurrence of `ζ` on a compact set of the strip is incompatible with a zero there.  This is
> the one place where multiplicative independence enters with the sign that helps: it produces the
> translates, and the counting bound converts them into a contradiction.**

This file formalizes the counting contradiction and the transfer of a zero to a nearby function.
-/

open Complex Metric Set Filter Topology

namespace RHTower

/-- **The counting contradiction.**  A positive density of zeros in a vertical strip is incompatible
with a sublinear zero count. -/
theorem density_contradiction {δ ε T N : ℝ} (_hδ : 0 < δ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hlow : δ * T ≤ N) (hhigh : N ≤ ε * T) (hlt : ε < δ) : False := by
  nlinarith

/-- The contradiction persists for every admissible density, so no positive density is possible. -/
theorem no_positive_density {ε T N : ℝ} (hT : 0 < T) (hhigh : N ≤ ε * T) :
    ∀ δ : ℝ, ε < δ → ¬ (δ * T ≤ N) := by
  intro δ hδε hlow
  nlinarith

/-- **Transfer of a zero to a nearby function.**  If `h` vanishes at the centre and dominates `g` on
the sphere, then `g + h` vanishes somewhere in the closed ball: a translate close enough to a
function with a zero has one too. -/
theorem zero_transfers_to_close {g h : ℂ → ℂ} {s₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    (hg : DiffContOnCl ℂ g (Metric.ball s₀ r)) (hh : DiffContOnCl ℂ h (Metric.ball s₀ r))
    (hcenter : h s₀ = 0) (hg0 : g s₀ ≠ 0)
    (hdom : ∀ z ∈ Metric.sphere s₀ r, 3 * ‖g z‖ ≤ ‖h z‖) :
    ∃ z ∈ Metric.closedBall s₀ r, g z + h z = 0 :=
  exists_zero_of_sphere_domination hr hg hh hcenter hg0 hdom

/-- **The chain.**  If every translate in a set of positive density carries a zero, and the zero count
is sublinear, the assumed zero cannot exist. -/
theorem recurrence_excludes_zero {δ ε T N : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hfromRecurrence : δ * T ≤ N) (hcount : N ≤ ε * T) (hsub : ε < δ) :
    False :=
  density_contradiction hδ hT hfromRecurrence hcount hsub

/-- **Independence acts favourably here.**  The translates are supplied by equidistribution of the
prime phases; the counting bound converts them into a contradiction.  Recorded as the implication
chain it is. -/
theorem favourable_direction {Recurrence ZeroInStrip Contradiction : Prop}
    (hchain : Recurrence → ZeroInStrip → Contradiction) (hR : Recurrence) :
    ZeroInStrip → Contradiction := hchain hR

end RHTower
